title: 20-Minute Cheesy Scallion Ground Beef
dek: Deeply browned ground beef folded with smoky seasonings, sharp cheddar, and plenty of fresh scallions—a fast, flexible dinner for hectic nights.
image_alt: A bowl of seasoned ground beef mixed with shredded cheese and topped with sliced scallions
ingredients: 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
Warm tortillas, toast, baked potatoes, or cooked rice, for serving (optional)

instructions.name: Soften the onion
instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add onion and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until softened at the edges.

instructions.name: Brown the beef
instructions.text: Add ground beef and spread it across the skillet. Leave it undisturbed for 2 minutes, then break it into small crumbles and cook for 5 to 7 minutes more until browned and 160°F. Spoon off excess grease.

instructions.name: Season the skillet
instructions.text: Stir in garlic, smoked paprika, Worcestershire, oregano, salt, and pepper. Cook for 1 minute, scraping up the browned bits so the seasonings coat every crumble.

instructions.name: Fold in the cheese
instructions.text: Remove the skillet from the heat. Fold in three-quarters of the cheddar and half the scallions until the cheese melts into the hot beef.

instructions.name: Finish and serve
instructions.text: Transfer to a serving bowl and top with the remaining cheddar and scallions. Add hot sauce if you like and serve as-is or spoon over tortillas, toast, baked potatoes, or rice.

why_it_works: Leaving the beef alone for the first 2 minutes creates browned flavor before it is crumbled.
Worcestershire and smoked paprika make a short ingredient list taste slow-cooked.
Melting the cheese off the heat keeps it creamy instead of oily.
swaps: Use ground turkey and add 1 extra tablespoon olive oil while browning.
Pepper Jack can replace cheddar for a spicier finish.
Stir in 1 cup thawed peas or chopped baby spinach before adding the cheese.
storage: Refrigerate in a shallow airtight container for up to 4 days. Reheat individual portions with 1 tablespoon water, covered, until steaming and 165°F. Freeze cooled beef for up to 2 months; thaw overnight before reheating.
notes: A wide skillet gives moisture room to evaporate so the beef browns instead of steaming.
Drain only the excess grease; a little fat helps the seasonings coat the beef.
Add the cheese off the heat so it melts smoothly rather than separating.

faqs.q: What should I serve with it?
faqs.a: It works in warm tortillas, over toast, baked potatoes, or rice, or beside a simple salad or steamed vegetable.

faqs.q: Can I make it less rich?
faqs.a: Use 93% lean beef, reduce the cheddar to 3/4 cup, and add a diced bell pepper with the onion.
Yes. Cook 1 diced bell pepper with the onion, or fold in thawed peas or baby spinach just before the cheese.

title: Weeknight Chili Con Carne with Corn & Beans
dek: A thick, beefy red chili with two kinds of beans, sweet corn, and a properly bloomed spice base—ready in under an hour.
image_alt: A bowl of red chili con carne with ground beef, beans, corn, sour cream, and sliced scallions
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) kidney beans, rinsed and drained
1 can (15 oz) black beans, rinsed and drained
Sour cream and sliced scallions, for serving

instructions.name: Brown the beef
instructions.text: Heat oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high. Add ground beef and cook for 7 to 9 minutes, breaking it up, until deeply browned and 160°F. Drain excess grease if needed.

instructions.name: Soften the vegetables
instructions.text: Add onion and bell pepper. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onion turns translucent and the pepper begins to soften. Add garlic and cook for 30 seconds.

instructions.name: Bloom the spices
instructions.text: Add chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, oregano, tomato paste, salt, and pepper. Stir constantly for 1 minute, until the tomato paste darkens and the spices smell toasted.

instructions.name: Simmer until thick
instructions.text: Stir in crushed tomatoes, kidney beans, black beans, corn, and broth. Bring to a boil, reduce to a steady simmer, and cook uncovered for 25 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes so the bottom does not scorch.

instructions.name: Finish bright
instructions.text: Stir in lime juice. Taste and adjust salt. Ladle into bowls and top with sour cream and scallions.

why_it_works: Cooking tomato paste and spices in the beef fat removes their raw edge and wakes up their flavor.
An uncovered simmer concentrates the tomatoes into chili rather than soup.
Lime juice added at the end balances the richness without making the chili taste citrusy.
swaps: Use all kidney beans or all black beans if that is what you have.
Replace frozen corn with a drained 15-ounce can of corn.
For more heat, add 1 minced jalapeño with the bell pepper or 1/4 teaspoon cayenne with the spices.
storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate for up to 4 days. Reheat on the stove, stirring often, until steaming and 165°F. Freeze in meal-size containers for up to 3 months, leaving room for expansion.
notes: Chili powder means the mild American spice blend, not pure ground chile.
A wide pot reduces the chili faster than a narrow saucepan.
The chili thickens further as it rests, making leftovers especially good.

faqs.q: Can I make this in a slow cooker?
faqs.a: Yes. Brown the beef and bloom the spices first, then cook everything except lime juice on low for 5 to 6 hours. Stir in lime before serving.

faqs.q: How do I make it less spicy?
faqs.a: Use a mild chili powder, skip cayenne or jalapeño, and serve with sour cream. The recipe is moderately seasoned, not aggressively hot.
Keep simmering uncovered over medium-low heat. A broad Dutch oven usually needs about 25 minutes, while a narrow pot may need 10 minutes longer.

title: Creamy Ground Beef Stroganoff with Egg Noodles
dek: Browned mushrooms, crumbled beef, and a tangy sour-cream gravy cling to wide egg noodles in this 40-minute comfort-food dinner.
image_alt: Creamy beef stroganoff served over wide egg noodles and garnished with fresh parsley

instructions.name: Cook the noodles
instructions.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook egg noodles until just tender according to the package. Reserve 1 cup noodle water, drain, and keep the noodles warm.

instructions.name: Brown the mushrooms
instructions.text: Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Spread mushrooms in one layer, season with 1/4 teaspoon salt, and cook without stirring for 3 minutes. Stir and cook 3 minutes more until browned; transfer to a plate.

instructions.name: Brown the beef
instructions.text: Add ground beef and onion to the skillet. Cook for 7 to 9 minutes, breaking the beef into small pieces, until browned and 160°F. Spoon off excess grease. Add garlic and cook for 30 seconds.

instructions.name: Build the gravy
instructions.text: Sprinkle flour over the beef and stir for 1 minute. Gradually add broth while scraping the skillet. Stir in Worcestershire, Dijon, remaining salt, and pepper. Simmer for 4 to 5 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon.

instructions.name: Finish without curdling
instructions.text: Remove the skillet from the heat. Stir 1/2 cup hot gravy into the sour cream in a small bowl, then fold that mixture back into the skillet. Return the mushrooms and toss with the noodles, loosening with reserved noodle water as needed. Finish with parsley.

why_it_works: Browning mushrooms separately gives them color instead of letting them steam beside the beef.
Flour cooked briefly in the skillet thickens the broth into a gravy that clings to noodles.
Tempering the sour cream off the heat prevents a grainy or split sauce.
swaps: Use white button mushrooms if cremini are unavailable.
Greek yogurt can replace sour cream, but temper it carefully and do not boil the finished sauce.
Serve the stroganoff over mashed potatoes instead of noodles for a gluten-free option when using gluten-free flour.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days. Reheat gently over medium-low with a splash of broth, stirring often, until 165°F. Avoid boiling after the sour cream is added. Freezing is not recommended because the sauce may separate and the noodles soften.
notes: A hot, uncrowded skillet is the difference between browned and rubbery mushrooms.
Full-fat sour cream is more stable in hot sauce than low-fat sour cream.
Keep the noodles slightly firm because they continue softening in the gravy.

faqs.q: Can I make stroganoff without mushrooms?
faqs.a: Yes. Skip them and cook 1 extra diced onion with the beef; the gravy will still work.
The sour cream was likely added to boiling liquid. Remove the skillet from heat, temper the sour cream with gravy, and keep the finished sauce below a simmer.
Make the beef gravy up to 2 days ahead without sour cream. Reheat gently, then temper and add sour cream before serving over freshly cooked noodles.

title: Classic Glazed Meatloaf with Garlic Mash
dek: A sliceable, juicy ground-beef meatloaf with a sticky tomato glaze and creamy garlic mashed potatoes—the full comfort-food plate.
image_alt: Slices of glazed beef meatloaf served with creamy mashed potatoes, brown gravy, and parsley
ingredients: 2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1-inch chunks

instructions.name: Cook the aromatics
instructions.text: Heat the oven to 375°F. Warm olive oil in a skillet over medium. Cook onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add half the garlic for 30 seconds. Spread on a plate and cool for 5 minutes.

instructions.name: Mix gently
instructions.text: In a large bowl, stir breadcrumbs and 1/2 cup milk; rest for 3 minutes. Add eggs, Worcestershire, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon pepper, and the cooled onion mixture. Add beef and combine with your hands only until evenly mixed.

instructions.name: Shape and glaze
instructions.text: Shape the mixture into a 9-by-5-inch loaf on a foil-lined rimmed sheet pan. Mix ketchup, brown sugar, and Dijon; spread half over the loaf. Bake for 35 minutes, add the remaining glaze, then bake 15 to 25 minutes more until the center reaches 160°F.

instructions.name: Make the garlic mash
instructions.text: While the meatloaf bakes, cover potatoes with cold salted water. Boil for 15 to 18 minutes until very tender. Drain and return to the hot pot for 1 minute. Melt butter with the remaining garlic over low heat for 1 minute, then mash it into the potatoes with warm milk, remaining salt, and pepper.

instructions.name: Rest before slicing
instructions.text: Rest the meatloaf for 10 minutes so the juices settle and the slices hold together. Cut into 1-inch slices and serve with garlic mash and parsley.

why_it_works: Soaking breadcrumbs in milk creates a panade that keeps the meatloaf tender.
A free-form loaf exposes more surface for glaze and prevents the beef from stewing in grease.
Resting for 10 minutes is essential for clean slices and a juicy center.
swaps: Replace up to half the beef with ground pork for a richer loaf; cook to 160°F.
Use russet potatoes for a fluffier mash or Yukon Golds for a creamier one.
storage: Refrigerate meatloaf and potatoes in separate airtight containers for up to 4 days. Reheat covered at 325°F with a spoonful of water or gravy until 165°F. Freeze sliced meatloaf for up to 3 months; mashed potatoes are best fresh or refrigerated.
notes: Do not knead or compress the beef mixture; overmixing makes meatloaf dense.
An instant-read thermometer removes the guesswork and prevents overcooking.
Warm milk blends into potatoes more smoothly than cold milk.

faqs.q: Why does my meatloaf fall apart?
faqs.a: It may need more binder or more resting time. Measure the breadcrumbs and eggs, mix evenly, and wait a full 10 minutes before slicing.

faqs.q: Can I prepare it earlier in the day?
faqs.a: Yes. Shape the loaf, cover, and refrigerate for up to 12 hours. Add about 5 minutes to the baking time and verify 160°F in the center.

faqs.q: Can I bake it in a loaf pan?
faqs.a: Yes, but the sides will be softer and the loaf may sit in rendered fat. Drain carefully and still verify 160°F.

title: Saucy Ground Beef & Rice Stuffed Peppers
dek: Tender bell peppers packed with garlicky beef, rice, tomatoes, and herbs, then baked in a bright tomato sauce until bubbling.
image_alt: Ground beef and rice stuffed bell peppers baked and served with rich tomato sauce and fresh herbs

instructions.name: Soften the pepper shells
instructions.text: Heat the oven to 400°F. Halve the peppers lengthwise through the stem and remove seeds and membranes. Arrange cut-side up in a 9-by-13-inch baking dish, add 1/4 cup water, cover tightly with foil, and bake for 15 minutes.

instructions.name: Brown the beef
instructions.text: Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add ground beef and onion; cook for 7 to 9 minutes, breaking up the beef, until browned and 160°F. Drain excess grease.

instructions.name: Build the filling
instructions.text: Add garlic, tomato paste, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper. Cook for 1 minute. Remove from heat and fold in cooked rice, drained tomatoes, 1/2 cup marinara, and half the mozzarella.

instructions.name: Stuff and sauce
instructions.text: Carefully pour the water out of the baking dish. Spread 3/4 cup marinara in the bottom. Divide filling among the pepper halves, spoon the remaining sauce around them, and top with the remaining mozzarella.

instructions.name: Bake until bubbling
instructions.text: Cover and bake for 20 minutes. Uncover and bake for 10 minutes more, until the peppers are tender and the filling reaches 165°F. Rest 5 minutes and finish with parsley.

why_it_works: Prebaking the peppers guarantees tender shells without overcooking the filling.
Draining the tomatoes prevents waterlogged rice.
Sauce beneath and around the peppers keeps the exposed edges moist while they bake.
swaps: Use ground turkey and cook it to 165°F before filling the peppers.
Brown rice or cooked quinoa can replace white rice one-for-one.
Use provolone or Monterey Jack instead of mozzarella.
storage: Refrigerate cooled stuffed peppers with their sauce for up to 4 days. Reheat covered at 350°F until the center reaches 165°F, about 20 minutes, or microwave individual portions covered. Freeze baked peppers for up to 2 months; thaw overnight before reheating.
notes: Choose peppers that feel heavy and sit steadily when halved.
Cook and cool the rice ahead to cut active prep time.
Pack the filling lightly so it heats evenly instead of becoming dense.

faqs.q: Do I have to cook the rice first?
faqs.a: Yes for this recipe. Uncooked rice needs more liquid and time than the peppers, so it can stay crunchy or dry out the filling.

faqs.q: Can I assemble stuffed peppers ahead?
faqs.a: Yes. Assemble, cover, and refrigerate up to 24 hours. Add 5 to 10 minutes to the covered bake time and verify the center reaches 165°F.
Red, orange, and yellow peppers are sweeter; green peppers have a sharper flavor and stay slightly firmer. A mix works well.
